# Field policy

<!-- Generated by scripts/records/gen-field-policy-doc.mjs from api/src/records/field-policy.js. Do not edit by hand: change the table, regenerate, and commit both. Input sha256: 24eda284f9e8909163be8cb071fad9a47764bb1904ffae0153bc3d1fc89f2696 -->

Who may change which field of a record on the website, and how. This page is generated from the policy table in [`api/src/records/field-policy.js`](../../api/src/records/field-policy.js), the table the API loads; `node scripts/records/gen-field-policy-doc.mjs --check` fails when the page and the table differ, and a test runs it. For why the table exists and how a change moves from the editor to the family tree, see [How editing and suggested changes work](../explanation/editing-and-proposals.md). For the routes that apply it, see [Family API: Editing API changes](api.md#editing-api-changes).

## The codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `direct` | The change saves now. |
| `proposal` | The change goes to review as a suggestion; an admin approves it. |
| `admin` | A member cannot even suggest it. Only an admin can make it on the web. |
| `desk` | Not editable on the web. It is done in Gramps desktop and syncs up. |
| `derived` | Computed by the server. A client write is refused. |
| `never` | Refused on every path, admins included (R-18). Gramps desktop keeps it. |

The columns are the viewer: `own` is a member editing their own record, `other` a member editing anyone else's, `admin` an admin. A pointer that matches no row is a `proposal` for a member and `direct` for an admin. The most specific row wins: a `never`, `desk` or `derived` row beats a plain one, then the pattern with more literal segments, then the row listed later.

Pointer patterns are RFC 6901 paths where `*` is one segment, `**` is any subtree (including the node itself), and `{a,b}` is a choice. A row with a condition applies only when the condition holds; with no way to judge the condition, the stricter row applies.

## Structure rules

These judge the ops of a whole submission, not one pointer.

| Kind | own | other | admin |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `birth-structure` | `proposal` | `proposal` | `direct` |
| `own-death-event` | `proposal` | `proposal` | `direct` |
| `custom-type-string` | `admin` | `admin` | `direct` |

## Switches for open questions (Q2-15)

Each row below is one switch that changes data, not code. The default is the first answer; `createFieldPolicy({ answers })` takes another.

| Switch | What it decides | Default (own / other) | Other answers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spouse-children` | Spouse and children on the own record (R-24 relationship proposals) | `proposal` / `proposal` | `owner-direct`: own `direct` |
| `own-death-event` | Adding, removing or retyping the own Death event (it changes the living classification, D2-08) | `proposal` / `proposal` | `owner-direct`: own `direct` |
| `custom-type-string` | A new custom type string (members choose only existing ones, DEC-E10) | `admin` / `admin` | `proposal`: own `proposal`, other `proposal` |
| `desk-list` | Desktop-only fields: Gramps IDs, private flags, LDS, group/sort/display-as, the place title (DEC-E8) | `desk` / `desk` | `admin-web`: admin `direct` |

## Withheld types

A row marked with a withheld-type condition fires when the value names one of these Gramps type numbers (the values of the Gramps type tables).

| Type | Withheld values |
| --- | --- |
| `AttributeType` | `3`, `6`, `10`, `11`, `12`, `14` |
| `UrlType` | `1` |
| `PlaceType` | `7`, `18`, `19`, `20` |

A Person link may be written on the web only as a Web Home URL, or a Custom URL whose string is one of `facebook`, `instagram`, `snapchat`, `tiktok`, `linktree`, `linkedin`, `website`. Every other URL type is `desk`, and an e-mail URL is `never`.
